sentences.text: The genus Elaltitan contains only one known species, Elaltitan lilloi.
It belongs to the parent group Lithostrotia and is classified within the class Saurischia.
Elaltitan is considered one of the largest sauropods ever to have existed.
Estimates of its weight have varied significantly, ranging from 35.4 tonnes to 42.8 tonnes, though a 2020 study suggested a size of 20 meters and 23 tonnes.
It is the first titanosaur skeleton known to preserve an associated calcaneum, a bone in the hind foot.
Philip D. Mannion and Alejandro Otero first described and named the genus in 2012, with the species name lilloi honoring Miguel Lillo for his contributions to natural sciences in Tucumán.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — dates to the middle Cenomanian to Turonian stage and was collected by an expedition led by José Fernando Bonaparte.
Fossils of Elaltitan are found in the Late Cretaceous of Chubut Province, southern Argentina.
The Paleobi Database records the time range for Elaltitan as the Coniacian stage, from 89.8 to 85.7 million years ago.
Before its formal description, the holotype of Elaltitan was originally attributed to Antarctosaurus sp. and later tentatively referred to Argyrosaurus.
